facts.text: Acres Green, built by Morris General Contractors in 1971 on a former pasture south of County Line Road near I‑25, was northern Douglas County’s first housing development.
The Acres Green Homeowners' Association, formed as a civic group in 1973, still enforces architectural standards through its Architectural Control Committee.
The community has successfully blocked industrial and high‑density projects, preserving its residential character.
By the late 1970s, Acres Green already boasted a park, an elementary school, and a library.
Before the 20th century, the land that is now Acres Green was part of vast ranching holdings used by early homesteaders.
Railroads like the Denver and Rio Grande line reached nearby Sedalia in 1871, and the Highline Canal was finished in 1883, boosting local agriculture.
